title: Tequila in India Moves From Shots to Slow, Premium Sipping
excerpt: Category sales nearly doubled in a year, agave bars are stocking 30-plus labels, and Indian investors — including a Shah Rukh Khan-backed brand — are buying into premium tequila.
body:
• India's tequila category grew 26% year-on-year, per IWSR figures reported by Storyboard18, with case sales rising from 68,200 in 2022 to nearly 123,000 in 2023.
  • The growth is premium-led: bartenders and brands describe a shift from party shots to sipping serves, with bottles in India ranging from Don Julio at Rs 9,350 upwards to Clase Azul variants above Rs 5 lakh.
  • Agave-focused bars are now a fixture in major metros — the Ritz-Carlton Pune's Agave Bar stocks more than 30 tequilas and mezcals, and one Delhi-Goa operator says 4-5 of every 10 cocktails he sells are agave-based.
  • Indian money is moving into the category: Radico Khaitan agreed to buy 47.5% of D'YAVOL Spirits — backed by Aryan Khan, Shah Rukh Khan and Nikhil Kamath — for up to Rs 40 crore, with a luxury bottled-in-origin tequila as its first launch.

Tequila's reputation in India was built at the bar rail: a shot, salt, lime, done. That is changing. The category grew 26% year-on-year in India, according to IWSR figures reported by Storyboard18, and sales nearly doubled from 68,200 nine-litre cases in 2022 to almost 123,000 in 2023. The same reporting projects the category reaching $120 million in revenue by 2030, growing at a compound rate above 10% — projections, not results, but the direction is corroborated by what bars are actually pouring.

From shots to sipping

"The category is moving beyond its party-shot reputation," Sree Harsha Vadlamudi, co-founder and CEO of Loca Loka, told Storyboard18, describing to The Established "a clear move away from volume-led drinking toward experience-led consumption." Vadlamudi argues agave's sweet, herbal, peppery profile mirrors India's own flavour vocabulary. Vikram Ku, who leads Diageo's World Class India bartending programme, credits the arrival of globally recognised luxury tequilas with introducing the spirit as "a refined, sippable spirit rather than just a celebratory shot," and pairs it with Indian ingredients — Gondhoraj lemon, raw mango, coconut water, green chilli.

The bar programmes back the talk. At the Agave Bar at Aasmana, in the Ritz-Carlton Pune, tequila sommelier Vedant Uday Shetty oversees more than 30 tequila and mezcal labels, in what he describes as the widest collection in the city; his most popular cocktail, the Quiote, mixes reposado, mezcal, Aperol, grapefruit, chilli and yuzu, Outlook Traveller reports. Chef-entrepreneur Tarun Sibal, of Khi Khi in Delhi and Titlie in Goa, says four to five of every ten cocktails at his bars are now tequila- or agave-based, driven by the picante, the paloma and the margarita. Vikram Achanta of Tulleeho has founded what is described as India's first agave-focused club, the Tulleeho Tequila Club.

The premium shelf — and Indian labels

The price ladder tells the premium story. Don Julio, launched in India in 2023, starts at Rs 9,350; Loca Loka — co-founded by Vadlamudi with actors Rana Daggubati and Anirudh Ravichander, distilled in the Jalisco highlands — starts at Rs 5,250. At the top end, Clase Azul variants run from Rs 28,000 to more than Rs 5 lakh a bottle, and KOMOS sells across Rs 26,000-90,000. India also makes its own agave spirits — not tequila, which by Mexican regulation must be 100% Blue Weber agave from designated regions — including Maya Pistola Agavepura, from wild Agave Americana grown around Chittoor and aged and bottled in Goa, from Rs 2,695, and DesmondJi, a Goa micro-distillery brand dating to 2011, from Rs 800.

"A clear move away from volume-led drinking toward experience-led consumption."

— Sree Harsha Vadlamudi, co-founder and CEO, Loca Loka

Where the money is going

Corporate India is buying in. Radico Khaitan has agreed to acquire 47.5% of D'YAVOL Spirits for up to Rs 40 crore, valuing the company at about Rs 84.2 crore; its partners include Aryan Khan, Shah Rukh Khan and Nikhil Kamath, and its first launch is planned as a luxury bottled-in-origin tequila. For drinkers, the practical change is simpler: in Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, Goa, Bengaluru and Gurugram, there is now a bar in each city where tequila is served the way single malts were a decade ago — neat, explained, and priced accordingly.
